title.title: An operator with no hyperinvariant subspace
title.subtitle: Claim: a nonzero quasinilpotent operator whose commutant is a proper, closed, transitive algebra

beats.text: Schematic: operators commuting with $T$ move any nonzero vector near any other
So no closed subspace besides $0$ and $H$ is preserved by the whole commutant
Claim: such a $T$ exists, nonzero and quasinilpotent, on every separable $H$

achievement.label: Hyperinvariant subspace and transitive algebra problems
statement: \exists\, T \ne 0 \text{ quasinilpotent with no hyperinvariant subspace}
achievement.context: Before: Lomonosov (1973) when $T$ commutes with a nonzero compact; Banach-space examples only
achievement.note: Does not settle the invariant subspace problem itself

verify.detail: $T \ne 0$, quasinilpotent, with a transitive, proper, SOT-closed commutant
verify.ourCheck: We compared the Lean scope with the claim; we did not build it

sources.quote: Does NOT resolve the invariant subspace problem itself

plain: Usually an operator leaves some subspace untouched by everything that commutes with it; this one leaves none

steps: Build an operator whose powers shrink to nothing
Make everything that commutes with it move any vector near any other
So no subspace stays fixed by all of them

voice.text: The operators commuting with T move any nonzero vector arbitrarily close to any other.
Build an operator whose powers fade, whose commuting operators can reach everywhere.
Claimed: it exists on every separable Hilbert space.
